hint.audioOnly: If on, no video: just the avatar’s voice.
hint.avatarId: The HeyGen avatar identifier. Find it in the HeyGen dashboard: open the avatar and copy the code shown under its name (or in the avatar page URL).
hint.enableClosedCaptions: Show live captions of what is being said.
hint.enableRecording: If on, Tavus records the conversation. Turn it on only if you need the recording.
hint.faceId: The Tavus avatar’s face/appearance (the “replica”). In the Tavus dashboard go to Replicas, open the one you want and copy its ID.
hint.idleEngagement: What the avatar does during silence: “off” waits; “patient” nudges occasionally; “eager” chimes in often.
hint.interactivityType: How you talk: “CONVERSATIONAL” = speak freely; “PUSH_TO_TALK” = hold to talk.
hint.interruptibility: How easy it is to interrupt the avatar while it speaks. High = it stops as soon as you talk.
hint.llmModel: The AI model that “thinks” and replies. When in doubt, leave the default.
hint.llmSpeculativeInference: Speeds up answer generation to reduce waiting. Usually worth keeping on.
hint.llmTemperature: How free/creative the answers are (0–2). Low = more precise and repeatable; high = more varied and creative.
hint.maxCallDurationSec: After how many seconds the conversation ends on its own. Tavus default: 3600 (60 minutes).
hint.maxSessionDurationSec: After how many seconds the session ends on its own. Essential plan reference: ~1200s (20 minutes).
hint.palId: The Tavus avatar’s “personality” (voice + brain + behavior). In Personas, open the chosen one and copy its ID. If you fill the fields below (model, voice, etc.), this ID is created/updated automatically on save.
hint.participantAbsentTimeoutSec: After how many seconds to end if the person is gone (nobody talking/on camera). Default: 300 (5 minutes).
hint.ttsEngine: The service that turns text into speech. “tavus-auto” picks the best one for you — leave it if unsure.
hint.ttsExternalVoiceId: Only needed if you use an external voice engine (e.g. ElevenLabs): paste that service’s voice ID here. With “tavus-auto”, leave it empty.
hint.turnTakingPatience: How long the avatar waits before replying, to tell whether you have finished. High = waits longer (fewer interruptions).
hint.videoEncoding: Technical video format. Leave H264 unless you have a reason to change it — it is the most compatible.
hint.videoQuality: Video quality. Higher = sharper but heavier; lower = smoother with less latency.
hint.voiceId: The voice identifier. In the HeyGen dashboard go to Voices, pick a voice and copy its ID.
hint.voiceIsolation: “near” filters background noise and keeps only the near voice; “off” does not filter.
hint.voiceSimilarityBoost: How closely the voice stays true to the original (0–1). Higher = more similar.
hint.voiceSpeed: How fast the avatar speaks. 1 = normal; below 1 slower, above 1 faster (range 0.8–1.2).
hint.voiceStability: How steady the tone is (0–1). High = more uniform and predictable; low = more expressive but variable.
hint.voiceStyle: How much emphasis/expressiveness to add (0–1). 0 = neutral. High values can sound over the top.
hint.voiceUseSpeakerBoost: Makes the voice clearer and more present, closer to the original. Costs a little extra latency. Usually worth keeping on.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.summary: A standing view of how much assessment work is in flight right now.

steps.0: Read the counters as a snapshot: they follow the candidates already created by the calling system, not people you invite from here.
steps.1: Open Projects to change what an assessment measures, or Candidates to see where individual people are stuck.
steps.2: A figure that looks wrong is almost always a filter question. Reports is where you narrow it down.

projects.title: Projects
projects.summary: A project is one assessment configuration: what it measures, in which language, and where results are delivered.

steps.0: Create the project and pick its assessment type. Standard measures the competencies of a role; Potential measures only MTG and LAT. This choice is permanent once the project goes live.
steps.1: For a Standard project, choose the role. That decides which competencies the interview covers.
steps.2: Set the webhook URL if the calling system should be notified of progress and results, and the exit URL for where the candidate is sent afterwards.
steps.3: Activate the project. From then on the calling system can mint entry links for it; assessment type and role can no longer change.

participants.title: Candidates
participants.summary: Everyone who has been given an entry link for one of your projects, and where each of them got to.

steps.0: Candidates appear here when the calling system creates them. BEAI never invites anyone and holds no contact details.
steps.1: Follow the status to see progress: waiting, in progress, being evaluated, then completed or failed.
steps.2: A transcript is readable from "being evaluated" onward; the scored report only once the candidate is completed.

reports.title: Reports
reports.summary: Every completed evaluation, and the BARS scores behind it.

steps.0: Narrow the list first: project, assessment type, role and period all combine, and the counter shows how many filters are active.
steps.1: Open an evaluation to see each competency, its indicator scores and the verbatim excerpts they came from.
steps.2: Check reliability before comparing two candidates. A low value means much of the interview gave nothing to score, not that the person scored badly.

project.definition: One assessment configuration: role, language, competencies and delivery settings.

participant.definition: A person given an entry link for a project. Created by the calling system, never here.

assessmentType.definition: Standard scores the competencies of a role. Potential scores only MTG and LAT, from four fixed questions. Permanent once live.

roleCode.definition: ICO, FLL, MLL, BUL or SRX. Determines which competencies the interview covers.

frameworkVersion.definition: The competency catalogue a project was created against. Pinned at creation, so a later revision never rescores a live project.

lifecycle.definition: Waiting, in progress, being evaluated, then completed or failed. Reading rights depend on it.

ssoLink.definition: The short-lived personal link a candidate uses to start. Minted by the calling system through the API.

bars.definition: Behaviourally Anchored Rating Scale. Each answer is compared with written reference behaviours and scored from 1 to 5: 1, 3 and 5 are the written anchors, while 2 and 4 are used when the evidence matches neither of the two anchors around it. An indicator with no assessable evidence gets no score at all and is left out of the average.

competency.definition: One assessed capability. Its score is the average of the indicators that could actually be scored.

indicator.definition: One observable behaviour that makes up a competency. Each indicator is scored on its own evidence, and the competency score is the average of the indicators that could be scored.

excerpt.definition: A passage taken word for word from the transcript. It is the evidence an indicator's score rests on, checked against the transcript and never rewritten or summarised.

reliability.definition: The share of indicators the interview produced evidence for. Low reliability means thin evidence, not a low score.

apiKey.definition: A credential for another system. Shown once, at creation, and never retrievable again.

ability.definition: One permission on an API key. A key can do only what its abilities allow.

webhook.definition: An address BEAI calls to report progress and results. Signed, and retried if it fails.

avatarTemplate.definition: Reusable voice and appearance settings for the interviewer.

llmCost.definition: What the language model behind the interview costs. It is estimated from the turns and characters actually exchanged, never read off a vendor invoice. It is never expressed per minute: the model is re-sent the whole conversation on every turn, so the twentieth minute costs several times the first, and multiplying a per-minute figure by a session length gives a wrong answer. It is billed by a different vendor than the avatar minutes and is never added to them.

review.title: Session review
review.subtitle: What happened during this interview: timing, integrity checks and snapshots.

integrity.title: Integrity checks
integrity.none: No events recorded during this session.
integrity.coverageIncomplete: Some detectors did not start, so this session was not fully observed. This is not a judgement about the candidate.

cost.separateMeters: Avatar minutes and conversation-LLM tokens are billed by two different vendors on two different meters. They are shown separately and are never added together. Both are estimates: no vendor exposes a per-session billed amount.
cost.llmNotBilled: This session did not run on a model BEAI manages, so no token cost was recorded. That is not a charge of zero.
